candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.EICC.2
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Engage in written or spoken conversations as both a speaker and listener for different tasks and purposes, making meaningful connections within and across texts and to real life.
Skills:
- Engage in spoken or written dialogue as an author and audience.
- Make intentional connections within texts.
- Make intentional connections between texts.
- Make intentional connections beyond texts to other knowledge or experiences.
Observable behaviors:
- Participate in dialogues by sharing ideas and responding to others.
- Make connections between different texts during discussions.
- Relate ideas from texts to personal experiences or other knowledge.
- Use spoken or written language intentionally to communicate for various purposes.
Pedagogy terms: dialogue, author and audience, text connections, purposeful communication
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Speak and respond in dialogues for different purposes.
- written_production: Write to communicate ideas and respond to texts.
- procedural_application: Use dialogue skills to connect ideas within and between texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain connections made between texts and ideas during dialogue.
- comprehension_response: Respond thoughtfully to texts and peers in spoken or written form.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2
candidates.label: Engagement & Intention

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.CP.1.c
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Language
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Participate in discussions and shared projects by sharing your ideas, listening to others, and giving feedback.
Skills:
- Contribute ideas to discussions and shared projects.
- Listen to the ideas of others during discussions and projects.
- Provide feedback to others in discussions and shared projects.
Observable behaviors:
- Offer your own ideas during group discussions or projects.
- Listen carefully to the ideas shared by others.
- Give feedback to others about their ideas in a respectful way.
Pedagogy terms: collaboration, discussion, feedback, listening, sharing ideas
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Express ideas clearly during discussions and projects.
- procedural_application: Contribute ideas, listen to others, and provide feedback in group settings.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain your ideas and feedback during discussions.
- comprehension_response: Listen and understand others' ideas during discussions and projects.
Codes: 1.P.CP.1.c

Standard: 1.P.EICC.1.e
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Participate actively in a community of readers and writers by following group norms, discussing texts, sharing writing, listening to others, and giving and receiving feedback.
Skills:
- Develop group norms for participation in a community of readers and writers
- Discuss texts with others in the group
- Share individual writing with the group
- Listen to others as they share their writing
- Offer feedback on peers' writing
- Respond to feedback received on own writing
Observable behaviors:
- Follow agreed-upon group norms during reading and writing activities
- Discuss texts with peers by sharing ideas and listening to others
- Share individual writing pieces with the group
- Listen attentively as others share their writing
- Offer constructive feedback on peers' writing
- Respond appropriately to feedback received on own writing
Pedagogy terms: community of readers and writers, group norms, discussion, sharing writing, listening, feedback
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Discuss texts with peers and share writing aloud
- procedural_application: Follow group norms during reading and writing activities
- reasoning_explanation: Offer and respond to feedback on writing
- comprehension_response: Listen attentively to others' writing and participate in text discussions
Codes: 1.P.EICC.1.e

Standard: 1.P.CP.1.d
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Comprehension, Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Work together with others to talk about topics, ask and investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts.
Skills:
- Work with others to discuss topics.
- Work with others to investigate questions.
- Work with others to solve problems.
- Work with others to explore and create texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Participate in group discussions about various topics.
- Ask and investigate questions collaboratively.
- Work with peers to solve problems.
- Explore and create texts together with others.
Pedagogy terms: collaboration, discussion, problem solving, text exploration, text creation
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Contribute ideas and questions during group discussions.
- procedural_application: Work cooperatively with others to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and create texts.
- investigation_handson: Engage in collaborative inquiry and problem solving with peers.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain ideas and reasoning during group work.
- comprehension_response: Respond to and build on others' ideas in discussions.
Codes: 1.P.CP.1.d

Standard: 1.P.CP.1
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Language
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Work together with others to achieve shared goals and complete projects.
Skills:
- Arrive prepared to actively participate in group discussions and collaborative meetings.
- Collaborate with others to determine group norms, establish goals and procedures, and facilitate productivity when working on shared projects.
- Contribute to discussions and shared projects by offering ideas, listening to the ideas of others, and providing feedback.
- Work with others to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Come prepared to participate actively in group discussions and meetings.
- Help set group rules, goals, and procedures to keep the group productive.
- Share ideas, listen to others, and give feedback during discussions and projects.
- Collaborate to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and create texts.
Pedagogy terms: collaboration, group discussion, shared goals, feedback, active participation
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Contribute ideas and provide feedback during group discussions.
- procedural_application: Participate in establishing group norms, goals, and procedures for shared projects.
- investigation_handson: Work with others to investigate questions and solve problems.
- comprehension_response: Listen to and consider the ideas of others during collaboration.
Codes: 1.P.CP.1
candidates.label: Collaboration

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.RA.1.c
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Students share relevant and accurate information using different ways to communicate.
Skills:
- Share relevant information about a topic.
- Share accurate information about a topic.
- Use a variety of communication modes to share information.
Observable behaviors:
- Use spoken words to share information clearly.
- Use drawings or pictures to communicate ideas.
- Use writing or digital tools to share information.
- Choose different ways to present information depending on the situation.
Pedagogy terms: share information, communication modes, relevant information, accurate information
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Share information clearly using spoken language.
- written_production: Share information clearly using writing or drawing.
- procedural_application: Use different communication modes to share information appropriately.
Codes: 1.T.RA.1.c

Standard: 1.T.C.2
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Identify who is speaking or telling the story at different points in a text.
Skills:
- Identify who is speaking at various points in a text.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out the speaker or narrator in a story.
- Recognize changes in who is speaking during a text.
- Name the person or character telling the story at various parts.
Pedagogy terms: speaker identification, narrator, point of view, text roles
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the speaker or narrator in a text.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain who is speaking at different points in a text.
- comprehension_response: Respond to questions about who is telling the story.
Codes: 1.T.C.2
candidates.label: Authors & Speakers

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.ST.1
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Use knowledge of important context elements like background information, location, culture, time period, and current events to understand and create texts.
Skills:
- Use prior knowledge, research, and discussions to identify key context components.
- Consider how context impacts the purposes of the author and the audience.
- Explore how context shapes the author's decisions and the audience's responses during text interpretation and construction.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify key context components such as background information, geographic location, cultural influences, time period, and contemporary events when reading or discussing texts.
- Explain how context affects the author's purpose and the audience's understanding.
- Discuss how context influences the author's choices and the audience's reactions during reading and writing.
Pedagogy terms: context, author's purpose, audience, interpretation, construction, background knowledge
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify key components of context relevant to a text.
- oral_production: Discuss how context affects author and audience purposes and responses.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of context to interpret and construct texts.
- investigation_handson: Use prior knowledge, research, and discussions to gather context information.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how context shapes author decisions and audience responses.
- comprehension_response: Interpret texts using understanding of context components.
Codes: 1.P.ST.1
candidates.label: Context

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.T.1.c
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Describe the main characters' traits and explain how their words and actions support the story's central message, lesson, or moral.
Skills:
- Describe traits of the main characters.
- Explain how the characters' words support the central message, lesson, or moral.
- Explain how the characters' actions support the central message, lesson, or moral.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify main characters in a story.
- Describe traits of main characters.
- Explain how characters' words and actions relate to the story's message, lesson, or moral.
Pedagogy terms: main characters, character traits, central message, lesson, moral, words and actions, explanation
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify main characters and their traits in a story.
- oral_production: Explain orally how characters' words and actions support the story's message, lesson, or moral.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how the characters' words and actions support the central message, lesson, or moral of the story.
- comprehension_response: Describe traits of main characters and explain their connection to the story's message, lesson, or moral.
Codes: 1.T.T.1.c

Standard: 1.T.T.1.a
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK1_recall_reproduction
Competency: Identify story elements such as characters, setting, major events, and dialogue used to craft stories.
Skills:
- Identify characters used to craft a story.
- Identify the setting used to craft a story.
- Identify major events used to craft a story.
- Identify dialogue used to craft a story.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out characters in a story.
- Describe the setting of a story.
- Identify major events in a story.
- Recognize dialogue between characters in a story.
Pedagogy terms: characters, setting, major events, dialogue, story elements
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify story elements such as characters, setting, major events, and dialogue in a story.
Codes: 1.T.T.1.a
